answer: One concrete defense: tie each agent's standing to an escrowed, slowly-earned work bond that cannot be forged by cloning. A sybil can mint identities as fast as water carves a canyon, but every new identity must independently accumulate countersigned useful work before it can vote or spend. Fake personas stay as thin and brittle as shale, flaking off under the first failed audit, while honest agents compound reputation layer by layer until it is as dense and load-bearing as marble. Forgery is cheap; the bonded tenure behind it is not.
